attractions.name: Raja Bazaar

attractions.name: Ayub National Park

weather_info.climate_type: Humid subtropical climate, similar to neighboring Islamabad, milder than Punjab's plains cities
weather_info.avoid_months: June-July (hot, humid before and during monsoon)

seasonal_notes.avg_condition: Heavy rain spells, occasional urban flooding in low areas

travel_tips.tip: Use the IJP Road or Islamabad Expressway to move between Rawalpindi and Islamabad instead of local roads during peak hours.
The Metrobus is the easiest and cheapest way to travel between Rawalpindi and Islamabad -- much faster than driving during rush hour.
Raja Bazaar can get very crowded, especially in the evenings -- keep valuables secure.
Visit Raja Bazaar in the morning for a calmer experience, and Committee Chowk food street in the evening when it's liveliest.

history.founded: Ancient settlement dating back over 2,000 years, historically linked to the nearby Gandhara civilization
history.city_history: Rawalpindi grew into prominence under British colonial rule as a major military garrison town, a role it retains today as the headquarters of the Pakistan Army. Often called 'Pindi', it functions as a twin city to Islamabad, with a much older and more traditional character reflected in areas like Raja Bazaar.
history.province_history: Punjab, meaning 'land of five rivers', has one of the longest continuous histories in South Asia, home to the ancient Indus Valley Civilization (Harappa), later ruled by the Mauryas, Mughals, Sikh Empire, and the British before becoming part of Pakistan in 1947.
